propositions: The lifespan shutdown drain awaits only queue.join() and covers webhook-queued reviews, but reconcile_once awaits review_and_vote inline outside the queue, so in-flight reconciler reviews are cancelled within shutdown_cancel_seconds (~10s) rather than drained.
Any container stop path that is not autodeploy (docker compose restart, manual deploy, host reboot, rollback) kills an in-flight reconciler review with effectively no drain time.
The reconciler retries reviews killed by other processes, but cancelled reviews emit no error and trigger no restart counter, making the gap silent and difficult to detect.
The drain must not extend indefinitely by allowing new reconciler reviews to start after shutdown begins; a stop-accepting-new-work signal is required alongside the budget-bounded drain.

The fix waits on in-flight reconciler reviews under the existing shutdown_drain_seconds() budget before cancelling tasks, sharing the deadline with the queue drain so the grace period relationship (floor 1260s against 1320s stop_grace_period) remains valid.
